description: A music video cut to a soundtrack that never touches a chain. The long-take way to film a song - one chained generation lip-synced end to end - degrades with every carried segment and can let the sync slip. This builds the video the way music television does instead: MiniMax-Music3 writes the song, one 'slice_audio' step per entry of 'shots' cuts it into frame-exact pieces (each entry's 'num_frames' at 24 fps, from its 'start_frame' less its 'lead_frames' of run-up), and one shot per entry is generated fresh from the same Z-Image portrait plus its own slice, lip-synced to just that piece. Each entry is {name, prompt, start_frame, num_frames, lead_frames, cut_frames}, all required: 'num_frames' is the length generated, on H3's 17n+5 grid (124 to 345, an off-grid value is refused, not rounded), 'lead_frames' is a run-up of song before the cut that the model sings through and a 'trim_video' step then trims off, and 'cut_frames' is the span kept, so a shot can start mid-line without the mouth snapping into motion; an entry with no lead has 'lead_frames' 0 and 'cut_frames' equal to 'num_frames'. 'song' defaults to the written song and is overridden with an 'asset:' reference to cut a song already on hand, which drops 'write_song' (it saves nothing of its own - the song is heard in the finished video). 'shots' is a list, so the cut is an argument: add an entry and there is one more slice, shot and trim, named for it ('slice@closeup', 'shot@closeup', 'trim@closeup'), and the loaded model is reused across every shot - identical pipeline definitions share one model. No shot conditions on another shot's output, so the last cut is as clean as the first. 'concat_videos' gathers the trimmed shots in list order, and because each kept exactly the frames of its slice after the lead, the edit is sample-accurate by construction: 'pair_audio' drops the original, unbroken song over the whole cut and the mouths line up in every shot. The soundtrack follows the list too - 'pair_audio' is given the whole song with 'fit': 'video', so it is cut to exactly the frames the edit came to, whatever length 'shots' is; a list long enough to outrun 'audio_duration' seconds of song is padded with silence and warned about rather than passing quietly. The generation models pass through one at a time - each is released before the next loads - so the workflow peaks no higher than its largest single model. Shots generated independently also drift in loudness - 10 dB between two shots of one scene is ordinary - and no seam control can hide a level jump, because it is either side of the cut rather than at it; 'match_levels' ('rms' for perceived level, 'peak' for the loudest sample) evens the shots out before they are joined, and left null, as it is by default, a wide spread is warned about in the log rather than passing in silence. 'audio_bleed_gain_db' ducks 'audio_bleed_ms'' full-scale bleed, left at 0 for no change. The singer's picture is one argument: 'singer_reference' is the <Picture 1> reference every shot conditions on, and it names 'draw_singer' by default. A standing cast member is used instead by passing a reference that reads a file - {"reference_type": "variable:image_reference_type", "from_file": "asset:cast/priya.jpg"} - which is the same shape 'dialogue-short' takes per shot entry. 'draw_singer' then goes unreferenced and is elided before the run, so the portrait costs nothing when one was supplied; it saves nothing of its own either way, being a conditioning image rather than a deliverable, and a portrait worth keeping is kept from the run that drew it. The soundtrack is peak-normalized to -3 dBFS on its way into the mux, and only there: Music 3 lands at or over full scale, and the mp4's second lossy encode had been pushing the finished video past it (#158, #159). -3 rather than the -1 an audio deliverable takes because the AAC encode in the mux overshoots by around 1.9 dB on this material where an mp3 overshoots by a tenth of one, so -1 was not enough headroom and the finished mp4 still decoded at +0.94 dBFS (#161). The slices that condition the shots are the song at its own level, untouched, so the picture is what it was.

vram_estimate.reason: Ref2VA holds every reference's encoding resident beside the video latents, so the ceiling is a fixed base, a per-voxel term for the VAE decode's conv3d activation (width * height * num_frames), and a per-reference term. Classified against the 24 GB entry from the #479 field report (lem, RTX 3090 24 GB, int4 + 768p turbo LoRA, 9 steps, 2026-09-25/26) at 1344x768: 175 frames x 2 refs, 209 x 2 and 175 x 3 ran (projected 22.83, 23.77 and 23.83 GB); 209 x 3 OOM'd in reference encode needing a further 5.1 GB and 260 x 1 OOM'd at denoise step 1 needing a further 4.8 GB (projected 24.77 and 24.18 GB). The refused allocations are lower bounds, not peaks, so this is a classification with about 0.2 GB of margin either side, not a fitted curve. bytes_per_voxel is unchanged from #324's calibration (job 282172105da1); base_gb drops 0.3 GB now the references are counted separately

detailed_description:
The target video is in realistic photographic style. [Shot 1] A wide shot frames a small nightclub stage: <Subject 1> stands centred at a vintage chrome ribbon microphone under a single warm spotlight, deep blue darkness and the faint silhouettes of a band behind him. He sings the vocal of <Audio 1>, his mouth moving in natural synchronisation with it, one paw resting on the microphone stand and the other loose at his side, swaying gently with the tempo. His tail sways in counterpoint behind him. The camera holds a static wide shot throughout, the stage lights unchanging.

overall_soundscape:
The song of <Audio 1> carries the shot. Under it, a low nightclub room tone, the soft clink of glassware far off, and the faint brush of <Subject 1>'s jacket as he sways.

num_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and MiniMax-H3 generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps; refused rather than snapped, because each entry's start_frame, lead_frames and cut_frames are laid out against its length and a rounded one would shift the cuts

width.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
